title: Effects of gallic acid and physical training on liver damage, force, and anxiety in obese mice: Hepatic modulation of Sestrin 2 (SESN2) and PGC-alpha expression.
authors: Sousa, Jaciara Neves; Sousa, Berenilde Valeria de Oliveira; Santos, Eduardo Pinheiro Dos; Ribeiro, Guilherme Henrique Mendes; Pereira, Ana Paula Maciel; Guimaraes, Victor Hugo Dantas; Queiroz, Lorena Dos Reis Pereira; Motta-Santos, Daisy; Farias, Lucyana Conceicao; Guimaraes, Andre Luiz Sena; de Paula, Alfredo Mauricio Batista; Santos, Sergio Henrique Sousa
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨没食子酸与运动训练对肥胖小鼠肝脏损伤、体力和焦虑的影响，涉及SESN2与PGC-1α表达及GA与GATOR2的分子对接，但核心是代谢与生理效应，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，且无AI/物理模拟方法。
abstract: Obesity and overweight are multifactorial diseases affecting more than one-third of the world's population. Physical inactivity contributes to a positive energy balance and the onset of obesity. Exercise combined with a balanced diet is an effective non-pharmacological strategy to improve obesity-related disorders. Gallic acid (GA), is a natural endogenous polyphenol found in a variety of fruits, vegetables, and wines, with beneficial effects on energetic homeostasis. The present study aims to investigate the effects of exercise training on obese mice supplemented with GA. Animal experimentation was performed with male Swiss mice divided into five groups: ST (standard control), HFD (obese control), HFD + GA (GA supplement), HFD + Trained (training), and HFD + GA + Trained (GA and training). The groups are treated for eight weeks with 200 mg/kg/body weight of the feed compound and, if applicable, physical training. The main findings of the present study show that GA supplementation improves liver fat, body weight, adiposity, and plasma insulin levels. In addition, animals treated with the GA and a physical training program demonstrate reduced levels of anxiety. Gene expression analyses show that Sesn2 is activated via PGC-1alpha independent of the GATOR2 protein, which is activated by GA in the context of physical activity. These data are corroborated by molecular docking analysis, demonstrating the interaction of GA with GATOR2. The present study contributes to understanding the metabolic effects of GA and physical training and demonstrates a new hepatic mechanism of action via Sestrin 2 and PGC-1alpha.
abstract_zh: 肥胖和超重是多因素疾病，影响全球超过三分之一的人口。缺乏身体活动会导致正能量平衡及肥胖的发生。运动结合均衡饮食是改善肥胖相关疾病的有效非药物策略。没食子酸（Gallic acid, GA）是一种天然内源性多酚，存在于多种水果、蔬菜和葡萄酒中，对能量稳态具有有益作用。本研究旨在探讨运动训练对补充GA的肥胖小鼠的影响。动物实验使用雄性瑞士小鼠，分为五组：ST（标准对照）、HFD（肥胖对照）、HFD + GA（GA补充）、HFD + Trained（训练）和HFD + GA + Trained（GA与训练）。各组接受为期八周的处理，饲料化合物剂量为200 mg/kg/体重，如适用则进行身体训练。本研究的主要发现表明，GA补充改善了肝脏脂肪、体重、肥胖程度和血浆胰岛素水平。此外，接受GA和身体训练方案处理的动物表现出焦虑水平降低。基因表达分析显示，Sesn2通过PGC-1alpha被激活，且独立于GATOR2蛋白，而GATOR2在身体活动背景下由GA激活。这些数据通过分子对接分析得到证实，展示了GA与GATOR2的相互作用。本研究有助于理解GA和身体训练的代谢效应，并揭示了通过Sestrin 2和PGC-1alpha的新肝脏作用机制。
